faq.a2: In the European Union, encrypted at rest and in transit. Each organisation is isolated at the database level. Anonymised cross-company data sharing is off by default and controlled from your settings.
faq.a3: Start with the free credits, paying nothing. If your team regularly burns several hundred credits a month, a subscription is markedly cheaper per credit and unlocks the automation features.
faq.a4: Yes. Interface, generated emails and documents (minutes, reports, exports) in German, French or English. Document analysis handles German-Swiss tenders as well as French-Swiss ones.
faq.q5: How long am I committing for?
faq.a5: For nothing. No framework contract, no setup fee, no minimum term. Subscriptions are monthly and end with the period.
faq.a6: A ticket system is built into the product: you write from inside the app and the reply lands in the same thread. In French, German or English.

m1.f1Detail: Tracking code, learned local rules, spam, keywords, Claude AI. Every email is routed to the right project in under a second.
m1.f2Detail: Conversation history up to 50 messages. Inline images resolved (cid:), attachments listed, one-click delegation and forwarding.

m3.f2Detail: Multilingual. Automatic language detection. Speaker segmentation where possible.
m3.f3Detail: Claude Sonnet 4.5 structures the minute by CFC LOT, with numbering, participants, decisions, tasks, deadlines. Export DOCX or signed PDF.

seo.title: CFC tender software for Swiss construction
seo.description: Extract line items from a tender spreadsheet, send price requests and compare supplier bids line by line. CFC and NPK nomenclatures recognised.

soumissions.lead: Extract the line items from a tender spreadsheet, send price requests to the right suppliers and compare bids line by line, without retyping a thing.
soumissions.intro1: A tender rarely arrives clean. It is a spreadsheet of several hundred rows, with mixed lots, empty columns, long descriptions and units that change from one chapter to the next. The project manager spends half a day turning it into a workable table before writing to a single supplier.
soumissions.intro2: Cantaia reads the document as it arrives — spreadsheet or PDF — and produces a structure of lots, chapters and line items, with quantity, unit and description. CFC codes and NPK nomenclatures are picked up when present; otherwise line items are grouped by material family, which is enough to start the price requests.
soumissions.b1Desc: The engineering office's file is read as is. Line items come out with their quantity and unit, even on documents running to several hundred rows.
soumissions.b2Desc: You assemble packages of line items and send them to different suppliers. Each request goes out with its own tracking code.
soumissions.b3Desc: Incoming bids sit as columns next to the line items. Gap to the best price, total per supplier, remarks and conditions for each.
soumissions.b4Desc: Suppliers who have not replied show up in the tracker. A follow-up is triggered from the screen, with the thread history behind it.
soumissions.s1Desc: Spreadsheet, PDF or an email with an attachment. The document is filed under the project and analysed in the background.
soumissions.s2Desc: The extracted list appears by lot and chapter. You fix a quantity, a unit, a description — corrections are kept.
soumissions.s3Desc: You pick the line items, then the suppliers. The email goes out with the item detail and a tracking code unique to each recipient.
soumissions.s4Desc: Replies file themselves into the table. You award the lot, and the accepted prices feed your internal price history.
soumissions.mockupCaption: Comparison view: unit prices aligned line by line, best bid highlighted.
soumissions.detail1: This solution is for general contractors, construction management offices and finishing trades who receive tenders to compare rather than to issue. If you handle between two and twenty lots per project and the comparison currently happens in a home-made spreadsheet, that is exactly the gap Cantaia fills.
soumissions.detail2: The prices you award do not disappear: they build your internal history, reused to place later bids in context. A CRB price reference acts as a benchmark while you have no history of your own on a given item.
soumissions.faqA1: Spreadsheets (.xlsx, .xls), PDF, and documents received as email attachments. Large files are processed in blocks, which avoids losing line items at the end of a document.
soumissions.faqQ2: Do CFC codes have to be present?
soumissions.faqA2: No. When CFC or NPK codes appear in the document they are carried over as they are. Otherwise line items are grouped by material family, which is enough to build coherent price request packages.
soumissions.faqQ3: How do supplier bids get back into the table?
soumissions.faqA3: Every price request carries a tracking code. When the supplier replies, the email is recognised and matched to the right request, then prices are extracted from the attachment and placed against the relevant line items.
soumissions.ctaDesc: Create your organisation, drop in a real tender file and look at what comes out. No credit card.

seo.title: Automatic site meeting minutes with AI
seo.description: Record the site meeting, get structured minutes with decisions, open points and owners, then circulate them as a PDF.

pv.lead: Record the meeting, get structured minutes with the decisions, the open points and the owners — the same evening, not the following Friday.
pv.intro1: Site meeting minutes are the record that counts when a decision is challenged three months later. They are also the task everyone puts off: a two-hour meeting, six pages of handwritten notes, and a write-up done from memory the next evening, once half the detail has already gone.
pv.intro2: Cantaia records the meeting from a phone or a laptop, transcribes the audio, then drafts structured minutes: attendees, items in the order they were dealt with, decisions taken, and open points with an owner and a deadline. You read it back, fix what needs fixing, and circulate.
pv.b1Desc: Transcription and drafting happen right after the meeting. The minutes go out while the discussion is still fresh for everyone.
pv.b2Desc: The same frame every meeting: header, attendees, numbered items, decisions, open points. Numbering carries over from one set of minutes to the next.
pv.b3Desc: Each unresolved point can become a task with an owner and a deadline, visible in the project rather than buried in a document.
pv.b4Desc: PDF export, sending to attendees from inside the app, and filing of the document in the project with its send date.
pv.s1Desc: A phone microphone is enough. Long files are compressed and split automatically before transcription.
pv.s2Desc: The audio is transcribed, then read back by the model, which identifies topics, speakers and decisions.
pv.s3Desc: The minutes open in a section-by-section editor. You adjust wording, add an item, remove what does not belong.
pv.s4Desc: Once finalised, the minutes are locked, exported as PDF and sent to attendees. The send date is kept.
pv.mockupCaption: Editor view: numbered sections, decisions and open points with an owner.
pv.mockupSection1Body: Slab L+3 poured on 18.03. Striking planned for 25.03.
pv.mockupSection2Body: Shop drawing awaited from the engineering office.
pv.detail1: This solution targets site managers and construction management teams running a weekly meeting with the client, the design offices and the contractors. The longer the meeting and the more people around the table, the wider the gap between what was said and what ends up in the minutes — that is where transcription changes things.
pv.detail2: The minutes remain a document you sign off. Cantaia produces a faithful and complete basis; the editorial responsibility — what is kept, reworded or dropped — is still yours.
pv.faqQ1: What language are the minutes written in?
pv.faqA1: French, German or English, regardless of the language spoken during the meeting. A meeting held in Swiss German can produce minutes in standard German or in French.
pv.faqQ2: What happens to the audio recording?
pv.faqA2: It is stored with the project, in your organisation's file space, and stays available until you delete it. The raw transcript sits alongside the drafted minutes.
pv.faqQ3: Can you start from handwritten notes instead of a recording?
pv.faqA3: Yes, for site visits: a photo of your notes is transcribed, including sketches and recorded measurements, and feeds the report just like audio would.
pv.ctaTitle: Send your next minutes the same evening
pv.ctaDesc: Record a meeting, let the transcription run, read back the result. No credit card.

seo.title: Construction schedule from tender — auto Gantt
seo.description: Generate a Gantt schedule from tender line items: durations, dependencies, milestones. Editing, A3 PDF export and a public read-only share link.

planning.lead: A Gantt chart built from your tender line items: estimated durations, dependencies between trades, milestones — then it is yours to adjust.
planning.intro1: The schedule is almost always rebuilt from scratch. Yet the line items already exist, quantified and priced, in the tender that has just been awarded. Between the two lies nothing but translation work: grouping items into tasks, giving them a duration, setting the obvious sequences.
planning.intro2: Cantaia does that translation. From the line items of a tender linked to the project, the schedule module proposes tasks grouped by phase, with a duration per task, the usual dependencies between trades — you do not tile onto a fresh screed — and the handover milestones.
planning.b1Desc: A first complete schedule in minutes instead of a blank sheet. You correct, which is always faster than building everything.
planning.b2Desc: The classic dependencies between trades are set by default, technical waits included, such as drying time before floor coverings.
planning.b3Desc: Move a bar, change a duration, add a task or a milestone. Undo and redo are available while editing.
planning.b4Desc: A3 PDF export for the site office wall, or a read-only share link for the client, without creating an account for them.
planning.s1Desc: The schedule starts from the line items of a tender already analysed in the project.
planning.s2Desc: Tasks are grouped by phase, with an estimated duration and the dependencies between trades.
planning.s3Desc: You correct the durations that do not fit your organisation, move tasks, and add contractual milestones.
planning.s4Desc: A3 export for display, or a public read-only link for those without a Cantaia account.
planning.mockupCaption: Gantt view: tasks by phase, dependencies and handover milestone.
planning.detail1: The generated schedule is not a signed execution programme: it is a starting frame. It is useful at bid stage, to show the client a credible sequence, and at site start-up, to phase the works without opening an empty file.
planning.detail2: The proposed durations rest on the quantities of the line items and on the usual technical sequences. They know nothing about your crew sizes or your subcontracting habits: those corrections are yours, and they stay in the project.
planning.faqQ1: Do you strictly need an analysed tender?
planning.faqA1: That is the main use case, because the tender supplies the line items and quantities. A schedule can also be built by hand in the same editor, task by task.
planning.faqQ2: Does the schedule update with actual progress?
planning.faqA2: Progress is entered per task and compared against the original frame. The drift shows directly on the chart, without keeping two files in parallel.
planning.faqQ3: Can it be opened in MS Project or Excel?
planning.faqA3: The export available today is the A3 PDF, designed for display and sending. The read-only share link avoids exporting just to show the current state.
planning.ctaTitle: Pull a schedule out of your tender
planning.ctaDesc: Analyse a tender, generate the Gantt chart, adjust the durations. No credit card.

seo.title: Daily site report — hours and delivery notes
seo.description: The foreman logs hours, plant and delivery notes from site with a PIN code. The office centralises everything and exports to Excel or PDF.

rapports.lead: The foreman logs hours, plant and delivery notes from site. The office finds them centralised, week by week.
rapports.intro1: Site hours still travel far too often on A5 sheets folded in four, collected on Friday, sometimes the following Monday. Delivery notes take the same route, when they do not stay in the glovebox. Back at the office, someone retypes it all into a spreadsheet before invoicing.
rapports.intro2: Cantaia opens a field portal reachable with a six-digit PIN, with no account and no installation. The foreman enters the day's report there: crew present and hours worked, plant and running hours, delivery notes with number, supplier and photo. The office sees reports arrive through the day.
rapports.b1Desc: A link and a PIN are enough. No account to create for the foreman, no app to install on his phone.
rapports.b2Desc: Hours are grouped by week and by worker, across all sites. No retyping before payroll processing.
rapports.b3Desc: The note is photographed at delivery, with its number and supplier. It can be found again when checking the invoice.
rapports.b4Desc: Excel export of hours for accounting, PDF export of delivery notes for checking supplier invoices.
rapports.s1Desc: The portal is enabled project by project. A PIN is generated and handed to the foreman.
rapports.s2Desc: The list of workers is recorded once per site, then offered on every report.
rapports.s3Desc: Crew, plant, delivery notes, remarks and weather. The report can be saved as a draft before submission.
rapports.s4Desc: Reports flow into the project and into the weekly view. The site manager locks the ones that are validated.
rapports.mockupCaption: Weekly view: hours per worker and per site, ready to export.
rapports.detail1: This solution is for companies that employ their own crews and invoice on a time-and-materials or measured basis. The gain is measured less in typing hours saved than in disputes avoided: an hour challenged three weeks later is settled with the day's report and the photo of the note, not with an approximate memory.
rapports.detail2: The hours captured also feed the project's financial tracking: set against the invoiced amount and purchase costs, they give a margin per site, without double entry in a separate tool.
rapports.faqQ1: Does the foreman need an account?
rapports.faqA1: No. He opens the site link and enters a six-digit PIN. The session stays valid for a week on his phone, so the code does not have to be retyped every morning.
rapports.faqQ2: What if the report contains a mistake?
rapports.faqA2: As long as the site manager has not locked the report, it stays editable. Once locked, only the site manager can unlock it for correction.
rapports.faqQ3: In what form does the office get the data?
rapports.faqA3: In a weekly on-screen view, with an Excel export for hours and a PDF export for delivery notes. Reports also stay viewable project by project.
rapports.ctaDesc: Turn the portal on for one site, hand the code to the foreman, watch the reports come in. No credit card.
